summary.name: TrustTunnel
summary.one_liner: TrustTunnel is a modern, open-source VPN protocol originally developed by AdGuard VPN that tunnels traffic over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 so it looks like regular HTTPS.
use_cases: Bypass deep-packet inspection and network-level VPN blocking
Hosting your own VPN server with a client app
Keeping VPN traffic looking like normal HTTPS browsing
Getting faster VPN speeds than stealth-oriented TCP-wrapped VPNs
Auditing or implementing a VPN protocol with open source code
summary.what_it_does: TrustTunnel is a VPN protocol that requires you to deploy your own server and then connect with a compatible client app on mobile or desktop. It uses TLS for encryption rather than a custom cryptographic implementation. Its transport is HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, so its connections are designed to be indistinguishable from regular HTTPS traffic. Instead of operating on packets like traditional VPNs, it gives each connection its own HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 stream and can buffer multiple packets before sending, which the page says reduces confirmation overhead and improves throughput.
notable: Traffic is designed to be indistinguishable from regular HTTPS, per the page
Uses TLS and HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 transport rather than a custom crypto scheme
Stream-based architecture with packet buffering to reduce TCP-style overhead
caveats: You must deploy and run your own TrustTunnel server before connecting
In some countries the mobile app is not available in the App Store, requiring an Apple ID from another country
